items.headline: Greed holds at 75 while Valuation remains 87; PRICE_DISCIPLINE stays active
items.summary: The AGCI live engine reads Greed 75/100 and Valuation 87/100. The regime remains Correction and the matrix condition remains PRICE_DISCIPLINE — Wait / Price discipline. There is no fresh weekend market session, so no artificial score change is inferred.
items.whyItMatters: Risk appetite remains elevated relative to the available valuation margin of safety. The weekend energy deterioration increases macro risk without creating a better aggregate entry point.

items.headline: Saudi East-West pipeline outage threatens a potential loss of roughly 4% of global oil supply
items.summary: Saudi buyers and traders told Reuters that if the East-West pipeline does not restart within days, Saudi export flows could fall materially. The route had been rerouting about 4 million barrels per day toward Yanbu while Hormuz was impaired; repair estimates cited by industry sources range up to several weeks, while available Red Sea storage is limited.
items.whyItMatters: The pipeline shutdown has crossed from a temporary operational incident into a potential global supply shock. A sustained outage would tighten crude and refined-product markets, increase freight and insurance costs and reinforce inflation pressure into the Fed meeting.
items.agciSignal: SAUDI SUPPLY LOSS RISK / HEDGE MODERATE / DO NOT CHASE

items.headline: Fresh projectile strike sets vessel on fire in Hormuz and forces crew evacuation
items.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a projectile strike on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire and requiring crew evacuation. Attribution was not confirmed at the time of the report.
items.whyItMatters: This is a new physical shipping incident at the same time Saudi Arabia's principal Hormuz bypass is offline. The combination raises the probability that the energy shock persists through transport, insurance and availability rather than remaining only a geopolitical risk premium.
items.agciSignal: HORMUZ PHYSICAL DISRUPTION / ATTRIBUTION UNCONFIRMED / SUPPLY-CHAIN RISK UP

items.headline: Iranian official says Monday Oman talks are not expected to produce a signed Hormuz agreement
items.summary: A senior Iranian official said the Oman meeting planned for Monday between Iran and Gulf states is not expected to yield a signed agreement on Hormuz governance. The talks continue, but key disagreements remain over navigation rights and Iran's demand to collect shipping fees.
items.whyItMatters: Diplomacy remains a potential de-escalation channel but does not yet justify pricing an imminent normalization of Gulf shipping. AGCI should treat any pre-meeting oil relief as tactical until physical flows and a binding framework improve.
items.agciSignal: DIPLOMATIC OPTIONALITY / NO SIGNED DEAL EXPECTED / DO NOT FRONT-RUN NORMALIZATION

items.headline: Speculators turn net long yen for the first time since February
items.summary: CFTC data showed non-commercial positioning in the yen moved to a net long 10,796 contracts for the week ended September 8, reversing a net short of 92,227 the prior week. The shift coincides with stronger expectations for faster Bank of Japan tightening and possible domestic asset repatriation.
items.whyItMatters: The positioning reversal increases the risk of a sharper JPY move if the BOJ validates tightening expectations. For dollar exposure and Japan-linked portfolios, currency hedging assumptions deserve re-testing rather than extrapolating the prior weak-yen regime.
items.agciSignal: JPY POSITIONING REVERSAL / BOJ WATCH / HEDGE ASSUMPTIONS

Hormuz: vessel safety, tanker traffic, attribution of the latest strike, diesel, freight and insurance.
Oman talks Monday: distinguish diplomatic headlines from a signed, enforceable navigation framework and actual flow normalization.
Fed 15–16 Sep: decision and guidance with the energy shock adding inflation risk to already-firm CPI/PPI.
AGCI Greed 75 versus Valuation 87: PRICE_DISCIPLINE remains active; no weekend score change should be inferred without a market session.
JPY/BOJ: positioning reversal and whether policy signals validate the move toward a stronger yen.
Mexico-U.S. trade talks: no new official material change since the prior cut.
AI/technology and real estate: no new development in the period crossed the threshold to alter the existing allocation thesis.
Travel: Gulf, Hormuz, Saudi Arabia and Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb risk remains very elevated.
